title: Rights and Responsibilities of Consumers
summary: A consumer is a person who buys goods or services for his own use or for use by others on his behalf (family members), and spends money to satisfy needs. Goods may be consumables (flour, sugar) or durables (TV, refrigerator); services include transport, electricity, telephone, banking, entertainment, repair and medical services. A retailer buying goods for resale is not a consumer, but a shopkeeper buying a shirt for himself is. The quality of goods can be checked before buying; the reliability of services cannot be checked in advance, and services cannot be stored.

Consumerism is a movement by consumers (individual activists and consumer associations) to ensure fair and honest practices by manufacturers, traders and service providers, and to create awareness of malpractices. It succeeds only when consumers know their rights and responsibilities. The Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (replaced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019) gives consumers six rights and provides consumer courts. Consumers are often unable to use their rights for lack of awareness.

(1) Right to safety — protection against goods and services hazardous to life and health (a leaking gas cylinder, sub-standard medicines, a doctor's negligence). (2) Right to be informed — about quality, quantity, purity, standard, price, date of manufacture and expiry, and safety precautions (a medicine without dates, or an MRP sticker hidden by a higher price, violates it). (3) Right to choose — to select from a variety of goods at competitive prices without pressure. (4) Right to be heard — consumers' interests receive due consideration at appropriate forums: in government policy, by business and in consumer courts. (5) Right to seek redressal — to get compensation, replacement or refund against unfair practices and defective goods. (6) Right to consumer education — to be educated about laws against unfair practices, the tricks of dishonest traders, how to protect oneself and how to file complaints.

'There can be no rights without responsibilities.' (1) Self-help — be informed and alert, not dependent on the seller; 'self-help is the best help'. (2) Proof of transaction — always obtain and keep the cash memo, bill, warranty or guarantee card, needed to make a claim. (3) Proper claim — do not make unreasonably high claims. (4) Proper use of products — do not misuse a product thinking it will be replaced under guarantee. (5) Be aware of rights and use them; check quality marks (ISI, AGMARK, hallmark), MRP, weight and expiry date. (6) Keep agreements and pay on time; do not tamper with meters. (7) Avoid pirated software and media and fake products; think independently rather than being carried away by advertisements; complain against unfair practices. 'To be heard' is a right, not a responsibility.

(a) Consumerism
(b) A consumer (also a registered consumer association or the government)
Kavita bought a medicine without the date of manufacture and date of expiry printed on the package. (a) Which right is violated? (b) What should she have checked?

(a) Right to be informed.
(b) The dates of manufacture and expiry, MRP and batch number before buying.

(a) Right to safety.
(b) Exercise his right to seek redressal — file a complaint for compensation in the consumer commission.

vsa: As part of the right to consumer education, what should consumers expect to be educated about?

(1) The laws that prevent unfair trade practices.
(2) The ways dishonest traders deceive consumers.
(3) How to protect their own interests.
(4) The procedure for filing complaints.

sa: How can consumers take care of their own interests and protect themselves from market malpractices — 'self-help is the best help'?

(1) Collect information about products, prices and quality before buying.
(2) Check quality marks (ISI, AGMARK, hallmark), MRP, weight, dates of manufacture and expiry.
(3) Insist on a cash memo and warranty card, and keep them safely.
(4) Read labels and use products properly; be aware of rights and complain against cheating.
What is meant by consumerism? Explain any one responsibility of consumers.

Consumerism is a movement by consumers to ensure fair and honest practices by sellers and to protect themselves from exploitation.
Responsibility — proof of transaction: the consumer must always obtain and preserve the cash memo and warranty card, without which a claim for repair or replacement cannot be established.
'Every consumer must demand a proof of transaction such as a cash memo.' Identify the responsibility and explain it.

The responsibility to obtain proof of transaction. A bill, cash memo or warranty card proves the purchase, its date and price. If the goods turn out defective, the consumer can claim repair, replacement or compensation only on producing this proof.
Explain the right to be heard and the right to seek redressal.

Right to be heard: consumers' interests must receive due consideration — they are consulted in government policy, business listens to their views, and they are heard in consumer courts.
Right to seek redressal: consumers can get replacement, refund or compensation for defective goods, deficient services and unfair practices, through the seller or the consumer courts.
la: Who is a consumer? Explain the various responsibilities of a consumer.

A consumer is a person who buys goods or services for his own use or for others on his behalf, not for resale.
(1) Self-help — be well informed and alert.
(2) Proof of transaction — obtain and keep cash memos and warranty cards.
(3) Proper claim — make only reasonable claims.
(4) Proper use of products — do not misuse goods under guarantee.
(5) Awareness of rights, checking quality marks and MRP, honouring agreements and timely payment, avoiding pirated goods.
Describe briefly the right to safety, the right to be informed and the right to choose.

Right to safety: protection against goods and services that endanger life or health — the seller is liable for injury from a defective product.
Right to be informed: to know the quality, quantity, purity, standard, price and expiry date of goods and the precautions in using them.
Right to choose: to select freely from a variety of goods at competitive prices without pressure from sellers.
Describe briefly the responsibilities of a consumer.

Self-help; obtaining proof of transaction; making proper claims; proper use of products; being aware of rights; checking quality marks, weight and price; honouring agreements; not buying spurious or pirated goods; complaining against unfair practices.
What is meant by consumerism? Explain any two responsibilities of a consumer.

Consumerism is a movement by consumers and their associations to protect consumers from unfair and dishonest practices and to create awareness of their rights.
(1) Self-help — an informed consumer protects himself better than anyone else.
(2) Proper use of products and reasonable claims — misuse or exaggerated claims are irresponsible.
